items.prompt: What does pitch mean?

options.text: how loud or quiet a sound is
options.why: That is volume.
Pitch is not about how fast sound travels.

options.text: how high or low a sound is

options.why: Pitch is not about how long a sound lasts.

hints: A bird's tweet and a lion's roar are very different.
One is squeaky and one is deep.
Think of notes going up a piano.
items.explanation: Pitch is how high or low a sound is. A mouse squeak has a high pitch and a lion's roar has a low pitch.

items.prompt: How can you make a drum sound louder?

options.why: Gentle hits make smaller vibrations and quieter sounds.
A looser skin changes the pitch. It makes the note lower.
Colour does not change sound.

hints: Volume depends on the size of the vibrations.
Bigger vibrations make louder sounds.
How do you make the skin vibrate more?
items.explanation: Hitting harder makes the drum skin vibrate more. Bigger vibrations make a louder sound.

items.prompt: Sort the changes. Do they change the pitch or the volume?
hints: Pitch is high or low. Volume is loud or quiet.
Changes to the string itself change how fast it vibrates.
Changes to how hard you play change how big the vibrations are.
items.explanation: Shorter, tighter or thinner strings vibrate faster, which changes the pitch. Playing harder or softer changes the size of the vibrations, which changes the volume.

items.prompt: Which change makes a guitar string play a higher note?

options.why: A looser string vibrates more slowly and gives a lower note.
A longer string gives a lower note.
Plucking harder makes it louder, not higher.

hints: Higher notes come from faster vibrations.
Think about tuning a guitar.
Which change makes the string vibrate faster?
items.explanation: A tighter string vibrates faster, so it plays a higher note.

items.prompt: You blow across the tops of four bottles. Which bottle gives the highest note?

head: Bottle
Water inside
figure.alt: Table of four identical glass bottles: A is almost empty, B is a quarter full, C is half full and D is almost full of water.

options.why: A has the most air. A long column of air gives a low note.
B has lots of air, so its note is quite low.
C has less air than A or B, but one bottle has even less.

hints: When you blow, the air inside the bottle vibrates.
A shorter column of air vibrates faster.
Which bottle has the least air?
items.explanation: Blowing makes the air inside vibrate. Bottle D has the shortest column of air, which vibrates fastest and gives the highest note.

items.prompt: You tap these four bottles with a spoon. Which bottle gives the highest note?

head: Bottle
Water inside
figure.alt: Table of four identical glass bottles: A is almost empty, B is a quarter full, C is half full and D is almost full of water.

options.why: B has more water than A, so it gives a lower note.
C has more water than A and B.
When tapped, the glass and water vibrate. More water makes a lower note.

hints: Tapping is different from blowing.
When you tap, the glass and the water vibrate.
More water vibrates more slowly.
items.explanation: When you tap a bottle, the glass and the water vibrate. Bottle A has the least water, so it vibrates fastest and gives the highest note.

items.prompt: Match each sound to its pitch and volume.
pairs: a bird singing in a tree
hints: Decide high or low first.
Then decide loud or quiet.
Start with thunder.
items.explanation: Bird song is high and quiet, and thunder is low and loud. A whistle blast is high and loud, and a purr is low and quiet.

items.prompt: In a set of angklung, which one plays the lowest note?

options.text: the one with the smallest tubes
options.why: Small tubes vibrate fast and give high notes.

options.text: the one with the biggest, longest bamboo tubes

options.why: Shaking harder makes it louder, not lower.
Colour does not change the note.

hints: Angklung tubes vibrate when shaken.
Big things vibrate more slowly.
Do slow vibrations make low or high notes?
items.explanation: Bigger, longer tubes vibrate more slowly. Slow vibrations make low notes, so the biggest angklung plays the lowest note.

items.prompt: Big vibrations make a ___ sound.
hints: Think about hitting a drum hard.
This is about volume.
It is the opposite of quiet.
items.explanation: Bigger vibrations make louder sounds. Smaller vibrations make quieter sounds.

items.prompt: A sound meter reads 35 dB in a library and 85 dB in a busy canteen. How many decibels louder is the canteen?
hints: Find both readings.
Louder by how much means find the difference.
Take the smaller reading away from the bigger one.
items.explanation: 85 take away 35 is 50, so the canteen is 50 dB louder. A higher decibel reading means a louder sound.

items.prompt: Lia holds a ruler over the edge of a table and twangs it. She makes the overhanging part shorter. What happens to the note?

options.why: A shorter part vibrates faster, so the note gets higher.
Changing the length changes how fast it vibrates.
The ruler can still vibrate and make a sound.

hints: The part over the edge is what vibrates.
Shorter things vibrate faster.
Do faster vibrations give higher or lower notes?
items.explanation: A shorter part of the ruler vibrates faster. Faster vibrations make a higher note.

items.prompt: Why do workers wear ear defenders near very loud machines?

options.why: Ear defenders make sounds quieter, not easier to hear.
Ear defenders are for protecting hearing.

options.text: Because loud sounds are always high-pitched.
options.why: Loud sounds can be high or low.

options.text: Very loud sounds can damage hearing.

hints: Ear defenders cover the ears.
They make sounds quieter.
Why would quieter be better near a loud machine?
items.explanation: Very loud sounds can damage the inside of your ears. Ear defenders absorb sound and protect hearing.

items.prompt: Which sound has a high pitch?

options.why: A roar is a low pitch.
A bass drum is low.
Thunder rumbles low.

hints: High pitch means a high note.
Think of a squeak or whistle.
Birds make tiny, high sounds.
items.explanation: A bird tweet is high pitched. Roars, bass drums and thunder are low.

items.prompt: A short, tight string makes a ___ pitch than a long, loose string.
hints: Short strings vibrate faster.
Think about the top notes of a guitar.
Higher or lower?
items.explanation: Short, tight strings vibrate faster, so the pitch is higher.

items.prompt: Tap the bar that plays the lowest note.

figure.alt: A xylophone with four bars of different lengths side by side: the second bar is longest, the fourth is next, the first is shorter and the third is the shortest.

hints: Long bars vibrate slowly.
Slow vibrations make a lower note.
Find the longest bar.
items.explanation: The longest bar vibrates slowest, so it plays the lowest note.

items.prompt: Label the parts of the guitar.

figure.alt: A guitar lying on its side. The head with tuning pegs is on the left, a long neck runs to the right, and a round body with a dark sound hole is on the right.

hints: Tap a label, then tap its number.
The neck is the long thin part.
The sound hole is the dark circle.
items.explanation: Strings run from the tuning pegs along the neck over the sound hole. The body helps make the sound bigger.

items.prompt: Dewi changes the length of a plucked string. She ranks the pitch from 1 (lowest) to 4 (highest). Complete the table.
head: Length of string (cm)
Pitch rank
hints: Look at the first two rows.
Shorter strings sound higher.
The rank goes up by 1 each time the string gets 10 cm shorter.
items.explanation: Each shorter string vibrates faster. The pitch rank goes up by 1 each time, so 20 cm gives 3 and 10 cm gives 4.

items.prompt: Ear defenders reduce noise by 25 dB. A drill makes 105 dB. How loud is the noise reaching the ears?
hints: Reduce means take away.
Start with the loud noise.
Take 25 away from 105.
items.explanation: 105 take away 25 is 80. The noise reaching the ears is 80 dB.

items.prompt: Raka plucks a rubber band gently and then harder. What changes?

options.why: Plucking harder does not change the speed of vibration much.
Length stays the same.
Harder plucking makes bigger vibrations.

hints: Plucking harder gives a bigger movement.
Bigger vibrations change one thing.
Is it pitch or volume?
items.explanation: A harder pluck makes bigger vibrations, so the sound is louder. The pitch stays about the same.

items.prompt: Sort each sound by its pitch.
hints: High pitch is a thin, squeaky sound.
Low pitch is a deep sound.
Imagine each one.
items.explanation: Whistles, mosquitoes and birds make high notes. Foghorns, bass drums and thunder make deep notes.

items.prompt: Wulan blows a recorder. When she covers more holes, the note gets lower. Why?

options.text: The air column inside becomes longer, so it vibrates more slowly.

options.why: Temperature is not the main reason.
Volume is not the same as pitch.

options.text: The holes make the air vibrate faster.
options.why: Covering holes makes it slower.

hints: More covered holes make a longer tube of vibrating air.
Long means slow.
Slower vibrations mean a lower note.
items.explanation: Covering holes makes the vibrating air column longer. Longer columns vibrate more slowly and make lower notes.

items.prompt: A ruler hangs over a table edge and is twanged. Complete the table with vibrations in 1 second.
head: Overhang (cm)
Vibrations in 1 second
hints: 72 and 36: the overhang doubled and the vibrations halved.
Multiply overhang by vibrations for the first row.
The product stays the same, 360.
items.explanation: Overhang × vibrations is always 360. So 15 cm gives 360 ÷ 15 = 24 and 20 cm gives 360 ÷ 20 = 18.

items.prompt: A ruler overhangs by 6, 12, 18 and 24 cm. It vibrates 60, 30, 20 and 15 times in a second. What do the results show?

options.text: The longer the overhang, the higher the pitch.
options.why: More vibrations a second means a higher pitch, and the longer overhang had fewer.

options.text: The longer the overhang, the fewer the vibrations, so the lower the pitch.
Overhang does not change the pitch.
options.why: The vibrations changed a lot.
The results show the pitch, not the loudness.

hints: Look at how the vibrations change.
Fewer vibrations a second is a lower pitch.
Compare 6 cm with 24 cm.
items.explanation: As the overhang gets longer, the ruler vibrates fewer times in a second. Fewer vibrations mean a lower pitch.

head: Overhang (cm)
Vibrations in 1 second
figure.alt: Table: overhang 6 cm gives 60 vibrations, 12 cm gives 30, 18 cm gives 20 and 24 cm gives 15.

items.prompt: Choose 2 ways to make a guitar sound louder.
hints: Louder means bigger vibrations.
Shorter and tighter strings change pitch.
Think of hitting harder and adding power.
items.explanation: A harder pluck and an amplifier both make the sound louder. Shortening or tightening a string changes the pitch.

items.prompt: Which instrument usually plays the lowest notes?

options.why: A piccolo is small and plays very high notes.
A flute plays higher notes.
A violin plays higher notes than a tuba.

hints: Large instruments have long air columns or strings.
Long means slow vibrations.
Which one is biggest?
items.explanation: The tuba is big and has a long tube. Long tubes vibrate slowly, so it plays low notes.

items.prompt: Match each change to its effect on the sound.
hints: Length changes pitch.
Size of vibrations changes volume.
Short is high, long is low.
items.explanation: Shorter strings vibrate faster and sound higher. Bigger vibrations make a louder sound.

items.prompt: Faster vibrations make a ___ pitch. Bigger vibrations make a ___ sound.
hints: Pitch depends on how fast.
Volume depends on how big.
Fast vibrations sound squeaky.
items.explanation: Pitch goes with the speed of the vibrations and volume goes with their size.

items.prompt: Put these sounds in order from quietest to loudest.
hints: Think about how far away you can hear each one.
A whisper is about 30 dB.
A jet engine is the loudest.
items.explanation: A whisper is quietest and a jet engine is loudest. Chatting and a motorbike are in between.

items.prompt: Two guitar strings are the same length and tension. One is thin and one is thick. Which gives the higher note?

options.why: A thick string vibrates more slowly.
Thickness does change the pitch.

options.text: The one that is plucked harder
options.why: Plucking harder changes volume, not pitch.

hints: Heavy things move more slowly.
Slow vibrations are low notes.
Which string is lighter?
items.explanation: A thin string is lighter and vibrates faster, so it gives a higher note.

items.prompt: A ruler is twanged over a table edge. Tap the part that vibrates.

figure.alt: A table on the left. A ruler lies flat on it and sticks out over the edge. A hand holds the part of the ruler that is on the table.

hints: The held part cannot move much.
The free end is the part that moves.
Look past the table edge.
items.explanation: The part sticking out over the edge is free to move, so it vibrates and makes the sound.
